_comment: Dependency-update automation, replacing .github/dependabot.yml when CI moved to GitLab.
Dependabot does not run on GitLab, and GitLab's own Dependency Scanning REPORTS vulnerable
packages rather than raising routine version-bump MRs — so it is not a replacement for this.
This is a faithful port of the Dependabot policy, not a redesign: weekly, grouped minor/patch
per ecosystem, the same two major-version refusals, and the same python ceiling. Renovate
detects manifests itself, so the eight per-directory blocks become package rules.
Air-gap-safe exactly as before: Renovate only opens MRs against this project. CI still gates
every bump (uv sync --frozen / npm ci), and the `security` job surfaces advisories separately.
NO automerge, deliberately. This repository has repeatedly found bumps that were green in CI
and still wrong: a python base image that built fine and could not START, a Tika major that
extracted EMPTY text without raising, and three separate exact-pin drifts. Every bump is a
_schedule_comment: NO internal schedule, deliberately. The GitLab pipeline schedule is the single source of
timing. With both, a cron outside Renovate's own window makes it run, decline to act, and
exit 0 — a green job that did nothing, which is the inert-opt-in shape this repository has
already been bitten by twice (EASYSYNQ_IMAGE_PROOF, EASYSYNQ_RELEASE). One clock only.

packageRules.description: python-minor-patch — the uv project at apps/api
web-minor-patch — the SPA lock at apps/web
contract-tools-minor-patch — the separately locked contract toolchain

reportlab is capped <5 — stamp_controlled_copy's byte-determinism depends on reportlab invariant mode; a v5 bump needs dedicated byte-output verification, not an auto-merge (closed PR #271). Minor/patch within 4.x still flow.
Mantine majors are a deliberate UI-lib migration (D4 — the SPA targets v7); a v8/v9 jump breaks the build and is its own scoped project (closed PR #266). Minor/patch within v7 still flow.

The API interpreter is pinned to 3.12 by requires-python (>=3.12,<3.13) and .python-version; moving it is a deliberate slice. A newer base does NOT fail the build — it fails at RUNTIME: uv cannot satisfy requires-python from /usr/local/bin, downloads a managed CPython into root-owned /root, and the image dies as uid 10001 (closed PR #448, which was CLEAN on all sixteen checks). Not a semver-major rule: the tag major is 3 on both sides, so 3.12 -> 3.14 is a MINOR update and a major-only refusal would not match it.
